recipes.name: Sautéed Swiss Chard
ingredients_raw: 1 bunch Swiss chard, stems and center ribs cut out and chopped together, leaves coarsely chopped separately
1 tablespoon fresh lemon juice, or to taste

steps.text: Heat olive oil and butter together in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Stir in onion and garlic and sauté until fragrant, about 30 seconds. Add chard stems and white wine; simmer until the stems begin to soften, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the chard leaves and cook until just wilted.
Sprinkle lemon juice on top and stir to combine; add Parmesan cheese and season to taste with salt if needed.

raw_recipe.headline: Sautéed Swiss Chard
raw_recipe.description: This Swiss chard side dish is easy to make by sautéing chopped chard with garlic, red onion, white wine, and lemon juice; season with Parmesan cheese.

review.reviewBody: A nice and healthy recipe for Swiss chard! For those who find it too bitter, try adding some heavy cream to the cooked vegetables.

Oh Man!!! This was GOOD! First time trying swiss chard, and there were no leftovers. Even the kids ate it! I fried up 2 slices of chopped up bacon with the olive oil/butter mixture and cooked the onions a little longer than called for in the recipe and the carmelized flavor gave it a nice depth. Also, I threw in about a half a cup of minced carrots with the onions because they were going to go bad in the fridge if I didn't. So I added the garlic after the onions and carrot were happy so it didn't burn. I will use this recipe again and again!!!

YUM. The best chard recipe I've encountered yet! It is said that chard is "the valedictorian of vegetables," because it's so high in so many nutrients. I added about 1/4 c of golden raisins when I added the wine, and let them plump as they simmered. The tiny bursts of sweetness were amazing with the slightly bitter greens. I never thought of using Parm with greens before, but it was wonderful! Thanks for the recipe - it's going into my recipe box!

This is a quite nice recipe. It's toothy and delicious. I cut the stems into matchstick size pieces and simmered them for 10 minutes instead of five minutes. I added a can of drained garbanzo beans (as was suggested by someone else) at the same time I added the leaves. This helped round out and make this into a very satifying and tasty dish. Thank you, DannyBoy.

I've made this with wine and it was good but I usually make it with a splash of worcestershire sauce and, dependnding on how much chard you are using, a tablepoon or 2 of balsamic vinegar for a fabulous flavor!!! When the Chard is cooked to desired doneness I then generously sprinkle real bacon pieces/bits and parmessan or asiago cheese over top. I then let the cheese melt a little and then serve. Alternatibely you could place the fry pan under the oven broiler for a couple minutes which would brown the cheese a little as it's melting. How you decide to melt the cheese its really up to you!! Both methods are equally delicious!!

Really good, very common way to make chard and other bitter greens. I added some brussel sprouts and blanched the chard before - it takes out some of the bitter flavor. Also, the stems don't take as long to simmer.

Oh, boy! Was this so delicious! I was given two large bunches of organic red Swiss chard and was searching for a good recipe when I came across this one. Since I had so much chard, I needed to double up on the other ingredients. I also had to make some minor changes due to what I had on hand, and took the suggestion of one person to add some bacon. How could I go wrong there?!
I chopped about 6 slices of bacon, browned it, drained on paper towels, and reserved about 1/2 Tbs of the drippings. I added the drippings to the butter and EVOO. It made a heavenly concoction!
The only wine I had was a good quality dry Marsala. I used it and was delighted with the flavor. I added a heaping tsp of Chicken Base for flavoring.
Instead of Parmesan, I had a bit of freshly grated Asiago cheese.
The end result was so good, but the next day, I decided to toast some slivered almonds and add them in! Perfection!
I am so happy with the results, and there is sooo much of it, I decided to freeze it and contribute it as a vegetable side for Resurrection Sunday! I have a good feeling that the other guests will love this as much as I did! 
Danny Boy, thank you for this lovely recipe! It stands well enough on its own, yet it lends well to a little creativity and is forgiving if one must make substitutions!

Ridiculously tasty! This was my very first attempt at Swiss Chard. I added some chopped golden shiitake mushroom and a tiny piece of smoked pork (not necessary, but Hey, I had it on hand) in with the fresh garlic and avocado oil (my saute' oil of choice). Do not skip the coriander and white wine-they are essential! I can't wait to make this again:)))

My parents and I had gotten some chard from my dad’s best friend’s garden. We needed something to make using it, so I found this recipe. The chard had already started wilting, which made the cooking part a little harder. I halved most of the recipe since my dad can’t have too much animal fat (butter, cheese, etc.), but kept the chard at the same amount, and replaced the lemon for a bit of lime (probably could’ve used a little more). I sautéed the onion and garlic (which I used a little more than the recipe called for since we like garlic in this house) longer than the recipe called for since my mom loves her onion caramelized. It was delicious (and I can’t taste very well XD) and we paired it with some leftover veggies from a cookout. We’ll most likely make this again if we get chard from his friend again. Trade some more coffee beans for garden vegetables XD
Super tasty, I tried it with port wine instead of dry wine and the onions caramelised slightly adding a creamy and sweet touch. Loved how the parmesan cheese takes thisc recipe to another level!

Our favorite recipe for swiss chard, and even kale. We receive an organic veggie bag weekly and were overwhelmed with greens this year. We were desperate to find a few recipes so we would not get bored. We stumbled on this one and now make it every chance we get. We add red pepper flakes, and sometimes veggie broth and cook it down for more depth of flavor.
So flavorful! Easy and pretty to look at
We planted Swiss Chard in the garden this year and it is yielding a great harvest. I found this recipe and it is awesome. Will definitely make again as we harvest the Chard. Thanks All Recipes!

It's definitely a healthy recipe. I see how the flavors pair well together. However, I did not at the end feel as though all the work I put into chopping and cleaning veggies paid off. It was ok, but did not blow me away. The red onion was a bit overpowering, although I did taste a bit of the wine and lemon juice as well.
I omitted the Parmesan - but it was delish!
First time my husband & I ever had Swiss chard. Delicious!
Delicious. Best Swiss Chard I ever had.

This was my first time to prepare Swiss Chard and it was really good. I did tweak the amount of onion and chard and just used a little beef broth instead of wine. Next time I will add even more chard and less onion. This is a dish we will make again.

I’m not usually a big fan of Swiss chard. I know it’s good for you, so I thought I would try this recipe. I have to say it was absolutely delicious. It came out very bright and crunchy and not bitter at all. I will definitely make this again and will add it to my recipe box. I added salt when I put the Swiss chard leaves in the pan and I also used a tablespoon more lemon juice than the recipe called for.
